condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

1.1 The gap analysis for three vulnerable northern target districts have been conducted. 1.2 The automated weather stations in the KRB have been visited and assessed. Technical documents on procurement of automated weather stations have been prepared. 1.3 Initial stakeholder consultation was conducted on a catchment strategy. The draft outline was prepared. 1.4 The review of mechanisms was conducted. The first round of trainings is ongoing in selected target jamoats. 1.5 PES feasibility was initiated. Activity to be started at the third year of implementation. 2.1 Agro-ecological services identification was initiatied and ongoing. Demonstration plots have been identified and selected based on the developed criteria in three North districts. 2.2 Natural resources mapping and Watershed Action Plan of 3 vulnerable northern districts drafted. Development of maps for vulnerable watersheds is initiated. 2.3 EbA interventions to be implemented at the third year of the project. 3.1 One Knowledge Management platform was supported by the project. Identification of other platforms is ongoing. 3.2 Establishment of the Impact Evaluation Framework is initiated and ongoing.

1.1. Current status of Water reforms in Kofirnighan River Basin, and gaps the project can address, identified 1.2. At least two weather stations are modernized with up-to-date equipment and relevant staff trained on installation, utilization, and maintenance of the stations 1.3. At least 50 policy and decision makers from the relevant government agencies and other extension service providers (at least 30% female) trained on mainstreaming climate risks for integrated catchment management planning 1.4. Existing coordination mechanisms on integrated climate-resilient catchment management identified and number of meetings supported by the project 1.5. An ecosystem service evaluation conducted, and scenario modelling of selected watersheds developed in target districts /jamoats. 2.1. At least one private extension service provider in each target KRB district supported 2.2. At least fourteen Jamoat Watershed Action Plans (WAP) developed 2.3. An integrated set of village EbA/SLM/CA and hazard risk reduction interventions identified 3.1. At least three knowledge products developed and disseminated within the existing knowledge management platform 3.2. The impact evaluation framework/tools developed to enable effective adaptive management of Ecosystem-based Adaptation activities.

1.1. Current status of Water Sector Reform in KRB has been identified. The project team throughout the year has been actively exploring the possibility of supporting the process and only in November the specific action plan and a round table meeting has been held by the World Bank and the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources in the Conference Hall of MEWR. During the discussion it was identified that the works in the KRB has been stalled and in December a subsequent meeting on water reform process has been held in Rumi hotel that was supported by USAID. During the meeting River Basin Council was created with the appointment of its head and its deputies. 1.2. The Weather Stations during the 2022 has not been modernized. However, the feasibility study and procurement of necessary equipment for the selected weather stations are currently ongoing and will be achieved during the 2023 reporting period. 1.3. In March 2022, a series of trainings on mainstreaming climate risks for integrated catchment management planning have been conducted with participation of 97 representatives of various local government and WUAs. 1.4. In June 2022, the Project has supported one conduction of coordination meeting on Water Sector Reform as well as the integrated climate-resilient catchment management in Rumi Hotel with participation of various international development organizations and representatives of ministries and agencies. 1.5. In September an initial analysis of Project’s need was assessed by an international consultant to further coordinate her work with the Project’s needs. During the visit of the consultant, it was identified that eco-system valuation has never been conducted in any projects in Tajikistan, therefore, in 2023 it is planned to recruit a local consultant to further assess the situation with the international consultant. 2.1. The Project has identified Water Users Associations as extension services providers in each target districts and current on-going demonstration plots will be handed over to WUAs. 2.2. 14 Jamoat Watershed Action Plans have been developed. 2.3. An integrated set of village EbA/SLM/CA interventions have been identified and have been integrated into Watershed Action Plans. 3.1. In 2022, the Project continued to support the web-site of the Committee for Environmental Protection under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan and subsequent use of the platform to further disseminate information regarding the EbA. The District Analysis and District Profiles have been drafted and submitted to CEP for review and approval for dissemination to the local governments of 6 target districts in 2023. The two documents will be as a reference hand-book for local districts. 3.2. Monitoring plan for current activities of the project is in place. The impact evaluation framework will be developed after the recruitment of an international consultant and consortium to measure the impact of interventions.
